I’ve written the companion as a new book for the Terlingua site, packed in one tar.gz to extract at the repo root. I couldn’t run the .NET content processor or the tests here, because the .NET 11 SDK download was blocked. Instead I checked every file against the compiler’s rules (front matter, slugs, ids, option counts, at least one correct answer, single/multiple types) with my own script, and they all pass.

What’s in it

Size: 17 chapters and 65 sections with 543 questions, about 580 KB of content.
Structure: sections follow the book’s own section order. Each has page pointers, learning objectives, an “In a nutshell” summary, a sources list, and often a short C# snippet.
Two sections the book doesn’t have: a foundations check on probability at the start, and a closing case study that runs a single engineering decision through the whole book.
Questions: most are set in software, DevOps or telemetry situations. Each explanation teaches the idea in full, so readers rarely need to open the book.
Quotes: explanations include 625 short quotes from the book inside “ ”. A script matched every one against the book’s text, with page numbers.
Answer positions: the UI doesn’t shuffle options, so I spread the correct answers across positions (171 / 168 / 156 / 140). One known weakness remains: the correct option is often the longest one.
Code: the C# snippets are illustrative, not compiled. They rely on four small helper functions defined in the first section.
Solutions PDF: your second PDF turned out to be the practice-problem solutions manual. I didn’t need it, since all quotes come from the main text.
File placement (paths relative to the repo root, nothing to delete):

README.md: one new row in the Library table, nothing else changed
content/books/statistical-rethinking/book.yml
content/books/statistical-rethinking/NN-chapter-slug/chapter.yml (17 of these)
content/books/statistical-rethinking/NN-chapter-slug/NN-section-slug.md (65 of these)
The book’s date is set to 2026-11-13, so it publishes on the next build.
